title: Generic ampleness criterion for smooth connected group schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-regular-scheme] and let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with geometrically connected fibres. A commutative group scheme means an $S$-scheme with multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group identities and commutativity; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Every geometric fibre is semiabelian: over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$ it fits into an exact sequence of fppf sheaves of commutative groups $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to G_k\to A\to1$, for some integer $r\geq0$ and a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme $A$ (an abelian variety); here $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication. Assume there is a dense open $V\subseteq S$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $G_V\to V$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], so it is an abelian scheme. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_G$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] which is symmetric: $[-1]^*L\simeq L$, with tensor inverse-image pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $L|_{G_\eta}$ is ample for every generic point $\eta$ of every irreducible component of $S$, then $L$ is relatively ample over $S$: for each affine open $W\subseteq S$, $L|_{p^{-1}(W)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Proposition 4.3 and its proof in Section 4.8, printed pp.142,144: the scheme-only generic-ampleness criterion invoked as Raynaud, Faisceaux amples sur les schemas en groupes et les espaces homogenes, LNM 119 (1970), XI Theorem 1.13. The citation [8] XI 1.13 in 4.8 is a bibliographic typo: [10], as correctly cited in 4.3. Raynaud original local WANTED; general regular-base formulation extracted from Deligne usage, agent responsibility.

proof.text: Cover $S$ by affine opens on which the invertible module $e^*L$ is trivial, using local freeness of rank one. Each such affine is Noetherian. By [rem-pc-regular-normal] it is normal and decomposes into finitely many open and closed integral components. These components are affine, regular and Noetherian. It suffices first to prove ampleness over these affine pieces; retain a chosen rigidification of $L$ on each piece. Work on one nonempty piece $T$. The prescribed dense open meets $T$ in a dense open, and its generic point $\eta$ is a generic point of $S$.

source.place: Local reduction; Stacks Tags 0569, 033M; trivialization of an invertible module.

proof.text: Every fibre of $G_T\to T$ is nonempty because of the identity section. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality] to the smooth group morphism: its geometrically connected fibres are geometrically integral. On an affine neighbourhood of $\eta$ contained in $V\cap T$, the group morphism is proper and the base is Noetherian. Since $L_\eta$ is ample, [lem-trf-noetherian-fibre-ample-neighbourhood] gives a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq V\cap T$ containing $\eta$ on whose inverse image $L$ is ample. This is also relative ampleness over $U$, by [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover] applied to the single affine open $U$ itself. Since $T$ is integral, $U$ is dense.

source.place: Proper abelian open and ampleness neighbourhood; Stacks Tag 0D2N, then Tag 01VJ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-symmetric-ample-power-extension] with $H=G_T$ and $M=L|_{G_U}$. Its base is normal integral Noetherian affine by step 1; its fibres are semiabelian by hypothesis, and $G_U\to U$ is proper. The line is symmetric by restriction and is rigidified by the choice in step 1. Step 2 gives exactly the required relative ampleness over $U$. Thus obtain an affine cover $T_i$ of $T$, integers $n_i>0$, and relatively ample rigidified lines $B_i$ on $G_{T_i}$ with specified rigidified isomorphisms to $L^{\otimes n_i}$ over $G_{U\cap T_i}$.

source.place: Raynaud XI Theorem 1.13: existence of an ample extension of a power of the symmetric line.

proof.text: For each nonempty $T_i$, the open $U\cap T_i$ is dense in $T_i$. Both $B_i$ and $L^{\otimes n_i}|_{G_{T_i}}$ are rigidified lines on the separated smooth commutative group scheme $G_{T_i}$ over the regular locally Noetherian base $T_i$, with geometrically integral fibres by step 2. Regard the scheme as an algebraic space. The specified isomorphism on this dense open extends by [lem-sfb-regular-group-rigidified-line-extension] to an isomorphism $B_i\simeq L^{\otimes n_i}|_{G_{T_i}}$. This uses the full faithfulness clause, not existence of another arbitrary extension.

source.place: Rigidified uniqueness, the comparison used in Moret-Bailly VI Proposition 3.1 and Deligne 4.2--4.3.

proof.text: Because $T_i$ is affine, $B_i$ is ample on $G_{T_i}$; the isomorphism in step 4 makes $L^{\otimes n_i}$ ample there. Unfold [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every point an affine nonvanishing open is cut out by a section of $(L^{\otimes n_i})^{\otimes m}$ with $m>0$. Regard the same section, using associativity of tensor powers, as a section of $L^{\otimes(n_i m)}$. Its stalk values and nonvanishing open are unchanged, and $n_i m>0$. Quasi-compactness is already part of ampleness of $B_i$. These same opens therefore prove that $L$ is ample on $G_{T_i}$.

source.place: Elementary positive-power converse directly from Stacks Definition 01PS.

proof.text: The affine opens $T_i$ constructed over all pieces in step 1 cover $S$. The morphism $p$ is quasi-compact, as part of finite presentation. By [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover], the ampleness established on every $G_{T_i}$ implies ampleness on $p^{-1}(W)$ for every affine open $W\subseteq S$, as asserted. For the empty base the affine cover is empty and the same statement is vacuous.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01VJ: locality of relative ampleness on the base.

proof_origin.place: Sections 4.1--4.3 and 4.8; corrected symmetric semiabelian route. Missing local Raynaud and Deligne originals are WANTED in report.md; assembly and explicit locality by Q124.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q124-e0848bace (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no files changed. Statement repair (E7) confirmed. Deligne, Lemme de Gabber (Numdam scan, read-only): 4.1 says the canonical line is symmetric and trivialized along the zero section; 4.2 extends it over a regular base, unique because geometric fibres are irreducible; 4.3 and 4.8 apply Raynaud XI 1.13 over a regular base whose smooth open is dense. The base item, stated for an arbitrary L on an arbitrary smooth connected-fibre group, is false. I checked the counterexample myself: over C[[q1,q2]] with psi(y)=q1^{(y^2+y)/2} q2^{(y^2-y)/2}, the Fourier recursion forces every coefficient of a section of L^n except a_0 into (q1,q2), so sections are constant on the closed G_m fibre and L is not ample, while the symmetric cocycle leaves n unit coefficients. The new hypotheses (symmetry, semiabelian fibres, dense open with proper G_V) are exactly the setting of Deligne. Steps: (1) regular implies normal and splits into integral components, with a rigidification from trivial e*L; (2) geometric integrality from the identity section, the 0D2N neighbourhood applied inside V∩T where properness holds, then 01VJ for relative ampleness over U; (3) every hypothesis of the new node is checked; (4) regular-base full faithfulness on the dense U∩T_i gives B_i ≅ L^{n_i}; (5) the positive-root converse follows in one line from the definition, so elementary is correct; (6) 01VJ locality, with quasi-compactness from finite presentation. New node lem-sfb-symmetric-ample-power-extension: statement-only, self-contained, stmt_deps match its citations, three kinds of search recorded, no SGA, Raynaud original WANTED. It is not a restatement (normal base, power, existence only) and duplicate greps for Raynaud, XI 1.13, semiabelian and symmetric ampleness found nothing. Edge cases: field, abelian scheme, empty base. Batch 5: the three trf citations (057J integrality, 0D2N neighbourhood, 01VJ locality) are generic scheme lemmas, not trace-formula or Poincaré steps; rigidified-line-extension reaches sec-trace-formula only through the definition def-trf-algebraic-space. All upheld. I accept the five tool_uses. That needs a repair note for the citer; it cannot be fixed in this delivery.
